consensus_summary: Elders primarily mean mature representative leaders of God’s covenant people; the twenty-four elders of Revelation are most commonly the whole redeemed people (often 12 tribes + 12 apostles), with common alternatives of angelic/divine-council beings, the 24 priestly courses, or a non-symbolic ecclesial office.
book_summary: Elders are leaders and representatives of the assemblies seated as a court around the throne, identified as the constellations among the host of heaven and their stars.
consensus_core_identification: Representative leaders of the covenant people; for the 24 elders, the redeemed people of God (primary) or heavenly-council beings (chief alternative).
book_core_identification: Constellations among the host of heaven and their stars, as the court of leaders/representatives around the throne.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus boundaries concern redeemed humans vs angels vs priests vs ordinary office; the book shifts the referent to celestial constellations/stars, a category those boundaries do not enclose.
material_contradiction: None with a single settled consensus core, since the identity of the 24 elders is itself unsettled; the constellation reading is simply not among the recognized options.
rationale: Minimum cores: consensus = covenant representatives / redeemed people (or else angelic council); book = constellations/stars of the heavenly host as that court. Throne-court and host-of-heaven language overlaps the listed divine-council alternative, but no consensus primary or alternative equates elders with constellations/stars. That astronomical identification is therefore absent rather than a narrowing, broadening, or direct replacement of a settled referent, so the relation is NOVEL.
strongest_objection: The book could be read as only a celestial specification of the already-listed heavenly-council/host alternative (same texts: 1 Kgs 22; Isa 24; Ps 89; Rev 4), which would make the relation REFINED or DIVERGENT rather than NOVEL.
